chunk: The cloud lets you trade up-front capital expense for variable, pay-as-you-go operating expense. Instead of buying servers months ahead and guessing demand, you rent capacity by the hour or second.
Elasticity is the ability to scale capacity up or down automatically as demand changes. It removes the trade-off between over-provisioning (wasting money) and under-provisioning (losing customers).
source: AWS Whitepaper: Six Advantages of Cloud Computing

chunk: Going global in minutes: deploy your application across multiple AWS Regions with a few clicks so users have low-latency access wherever they are.
Total Cost of Ownership in the cloud bundles compute, storage, network, power, cooling, real estate, and operations into one bill. On-prem TCO requires modelling each of those line items separately.
CapEx vs OpEx: capital expenditure is a long-lived asset (a server you own for 5 years). Operating expenditure is a recurring cost (the monthly cloud bill). Cloud converts CapEx into OpEx.
Design for failure. Assume any single component can fail and architect so the system stays available: multi-AZ deployments, health checks, retries, circuit breakers.
Loose coupling: components communicate through well-defined interfaces (queues, events, APIs) so each can scale and fail independently.
source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, Performance Efficiency Pillar

chunk: Public cloud, private cloud, hybrid: in public cloud the provider owns the hardware. In private cloud you (or a single tenant) own it. Hybrid splits workloads across both for compliance, cost, or migration reasons.
AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud (the hypervisor, hardware, facilities). The customer is responsible for security IN the cloud (their data, IAM policies, OS patches, network rules).
For managed services like S3 or RDS, AWS takes more of the responsibility (e.g. patching the database engine). The customer still owns access control, encryption choices, and network configuration.
IAM users represent people. IAM roles are assumable identities used by services or for cross-account access. Policies are JSON documents that allow or deny actions on resources.
Principle of least privilege: grant only the permissions needed for the task, no more. Start from zero and add permissions as required.
MFA (multi-factor authentication) protects against stolen credentials. Enable MFA on the root user, all IAM users, and federated identities.
AWS Artifact is the on-demand source of compliance reports (SOC, ISO, PCI). Customers download these to share with auditors.
Encryption at rest protects stored data; encryption in transit protects data on the wire. KMS manages keys for both. Customer-managed keys give the customer rotation and audit control.
EC2 gives you virtual machines you manage. Lambda runs your function code on demand without servers. ECS and EKS run containers. App Runner runs containerised web apps with no infra config.
EC2 instance families optimise for different workloads: M for general purpose, C for compute, R for memory, G for GPU, T for burstable.
S3 is object storage: durable, eleven nines, accessed by HTTPS. EBS is block storage attached to one EC2 instance. EFS is shared file storage. FSx wraps Windows / Lustre file systems.
S3 storage classes trade off cost vs retrieval time: Standard, Infrequent Access, Glacier (minutes to retrieve), Glacier Deep Archive (hours).

A VPC is a private network in AWS. Subnets split a VPC across Availability Zones; route tables and gateways control traffic. Security groups are stateful firewalls at the instance level; NACLs are stateless at the subnet level.
CloudFront is a global CDN that caches content close to users. Route 53 is a managed DNS service. Direct Connect provides a private, dedicated link from your data centre to AWS.
RDS is managed relational databases (MySQL, Postgres, Oracle, SQL Server, MariaDB). Aurora is Amazon's MySQL/Postgres-compatible engine. DynamoDB is managed key-value/document NoSQL.
AWS organises capacity into Regions (geographic areas) made up of Availability Zones (physically separated data centres). Edge locations host CDN and DNS endpoints close to users.
On-Demand pricing has no commitment. Reserved Instances and Savings Plans give discounts for 1-3 year commits. Spot Instances offer up to 90% discount but can be reclaimed with two minutes notice.

AWS Free Tier comes in three flavours: 12-month free (e.g. 750 hrs of t2.micro), always free (e.g. Lambda 1M requests/month), and short-term trials. Watch the meter so you don't roll into paid usage by accident.

Support plans: Basic (free, account/billing), Developer (8x5 email), Business (24x7 chat/phone, 1-hour response on production-down), Enterprise On-Ramp / Enterprise (technical account manager, 30-min response).

Cost Explorer visualises spend over time. Budgets alert you when you exceed thresholds. Cost and Usage Reports give you the raw line-item data. Tagging is what makes cost allocation by team or project work.
Trusted Advisor checks accounts for cost optimisation, security, fault tolerance, performance, and service limits. It is the first place to look when starting cost reduction.
